Senses.Explanation: By occasion of the feast, to celebrate and praise. Yangqi Fanghui reads the World-Honored One's long silence before the heretic as yielding himself to another, so the heretic's entry is a feast-day celebration, and Changqing Huileng, judging Jinniu's twenty years of dancing the rice-bucket before the hall, calls it much like celebrating the feast and playing to the table. Poshan Haiming, bidden to a feast for Śākyamuni's awakening, says the mountain monk can only celebrate the feast, draws a circle with his staff and asks if the assembly sees; Liangting Jingting, on the birth day, celebrates the feast by indicting the yellow-faced one in a single bill; Baiyu Jingsi closes on the one phrase and answers with Jinniu's own cry — 'children of the bodhisattva, come eat!'; Yinyuan Longqi asks what is said for the feast-day phrase now; Weilin Daopei seals the finished three-sevens with a feast-day celebration where no wish goes unfollowed; Tian'an Sheng takes the feast-day turn to post a battle-model for the children of the bodhisattva, single blade straight in; Zhufeng Huanmin at the Ullambana basin lets dragons and elephants feast on the full basin's harmony; and Chisong Daoling, thanking a governor, raises the feast-day celebration to prop the way.
